text:
Alexander Wennberg has played 13 of San Jose's games, missing most of late October and two more in mid-November, and he still has no goals. Three assists in 13 games is a long way from last season's 55 points, though he is right back in the middle of things at 20:17 a night.

Our numbers read the slump as a mix. He has 2.6 expected goals and zero to show for it, which usually corrects. But he's also pointless in five straight, and the chances have thinned out lately (2.2 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten against 2.5 usual). Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted this weekend that Wennberg is still not taking faceoffs, something to keep an eye on for a center.

His value has never been all scoring. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 85th percentile at taking chances away last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a signature: 22% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. The goal should come; whether he's fully himself is the bigger question.
headline: Wennberg is back in big minutes, still without a goal
